Outer driver waits 7 seconds, kills only its own detached probe session, and verifies a separately owned foreign process survived.

result.scope: Synthetic timeout boundary only; no actual Chrome, CI or root-cause diagnosis

blockingFindings.title: Version diagnostic can indefinitely block the original failure
blockingFindings.contract: Diagnostics must remain bounded and must not replace or prevent the original checker failure; outer test deadline must remain effective.
blockingFindings.reproduction: Original synthetic browser exits 23. Its --version process ignores SIGTERM. spawnSync timeout=5000 sends default SIGTERM and continues waiting; diagnostics had not returned after 7 seconds. Node synchronous wait also prevents its test timeout from interrupting this path.
blockingFindings.impact: A diagnostic-only assertion message can stall the CI test instead of promptly surfacing the original NOT_RUN/exit2 or other mismatch.
blockingFindings.recommendation: Remove the version subprocess (record the executable path/hash), or use a separately owned process with enforced termination and descendant/stdio cleanup. Increasing the timeout does not establish a hard bound.

otherReviewedBoundaries.conclusion: Single-quote escaping is correct; real executable is resolved, exec receives quoted "$@". Main flags and PID/SID remain unchanged by construction and the author fake-browser evidence.

Logger keeps at most 65536 tail bytes and continues reading after truncation. Metadata remains diagnostic NOT_RUN; exceptions do not mark acceptance PASS. Synchronous per-block file persistence can add I/O overhead but no intentional size-limit backpressure was found.

Logger inherits the original browser-owned session, and the unchanged checker scans/kills all owned session groups. Author fake-browser test verifies no live owned groups and foreign survival. This review does not claim a new actual-Chrome lifecycle acceptance.

Original browser-case assertions still require statuses 0/1. No main-case retry, new Linux skip, deadline increase, plugin/workflow or release mutation was found. Diagnostics only occur after a mismatched status; run() exceptions before return remain outside this newly instrumented status path.

limitations: No repository writes, full test run, CI trigger, actual Chrome reproduction or model/desktop test performed.
No claim that this diagnostic change fixes the original Chrome startup NOT_RUN; its root cause remains UNKNOWN.
The 7-second probe was forcibly cleaned as a synthetic deadline test, not an acceptance PASS.
